question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[4X+2].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}, & 0<x\le 1, \\ \frac{1}{2{x}^{3}}, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of the expected value:

$$
\text{E}[4X+2]=4\text{E}[X]+2
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we calculate the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot \frac{3}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{1}{2{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3x}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{8})|}_{0}^{1}+{(-\frac{1}{2x})|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =(\frac{3}{8}-0)+(0-(-\frac{1}{2})) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[4X+2] & =4\text{E}[X]+2 \\  & =4\cdot \frac{7}{8}+2 \\  & =\frac{11}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
